value.deck: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds persistent cross-session memory and local model execution via Ollama for Business and Enterprise tiers, bringing functional parity with VS Code.
shortVersion: GitHub Copilot's JetBrains extension now incorporates Copilot Memory, enabling cross-session persistence of repository context and user preferences. Concurrently, the integration introduces Ollama support, allowing local open-source model execution to serve completion backends on the host machine. Both features are restricted to GitHub Copilot Business and Enterprise license tiers.

The Ollama integration directly addresses compliance and privacy requirements by enabling code-completion workflows in air-gapped or data-sovereignty-constrained environments. However, the platform changelog does not specify the underlying state-indexing architecture for Copilot Memory, nor does it detail local resource requirements and latency implications when routing completions to Ollama.
value.plainLanguage: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now supports cross-session memory and local open-source model completions via Ollama for Business and Enterprise users.

keyTerms.meaning: A persistence mechanism that maintains project context and developer configurations across distinct IDE sessions.
A client-side completion backend interface that routes code-generation inference to locally hosted open-source model runtimes.

value.whyItMatters: This update eliminates a major capability gap between JetBrains and VS Code while enabling zero-data-egress development for security-sensitive or air-gapped enterprise environments.
watchNext: Monitor whether GitHub publishes architectural details or telemetry regarding local inference latency across specific Ollama-hosted model families.
Watch for enterprise policy controls detailing how cross-session Copilot Memory handles cache invalidation and data residency across shared codebases.
